questions.question: Explain image sampling and quatization. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Explain image sampling and quantization. [U]/[CO1] Image sampling (1 mark): Sampling converts the continuous spatial coordinates of an image into a finite set of discrete pixel locations. Image quantization (1 mark): Quantization converts the continuous intensity values of the sampled image into a finite number of discrete intensity or gray levels.

questions.question: Analyze the effect of dilation on an object. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Analyze the effect of dilation on an object. [An] / [CO3] Dilation is a morphological operation that expands or thickens foreground objects' boundaries in an image using a structuring element. — 1 mark. Can connect nearby objects, fill small gaps or bridge narrow breaks, depending on the structuring element — 1 mark.

questions.question: State any two characteristics of Rayleigh noise. / [CO4] [2x5 = 10]
questions.solution_html: • State any two characteristics of Rayleigh noise. [K] / [CO4] Any two characteristics 2 marks- It follows a Rayleigh probability distribution. Its probability distribution is non-negative asymmetric, right-skewed. used to model certain types of noise encountered in radar and ultrasound imaging. Its statistical characteristics depend on the scale parameter of the distribution. [2x5 = 10] Part B, Short Answer Questions, Answer any 5 questions, Each question carries 6 marks

questions.question: State the objectives of histogram equalization. Explain how it improves the contrast of a low-contrast image. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • State the objectives of histogram equalization. Explain how it improves the contrast of a low-contrast image. Objectives of histogram equalization 3 marks, Histogram equalization improves its contrast through the following steps: Calculate the histogram: Determine the frequency of each intensity level in the image. Compute the cumulative distribution function (CDF): Calculate the cumulative sum of the normalized histogram values.Transform pixel intensities: Use the CDF to map the original intensity values to new values distributed across a wider intensity range. 3 Marks. [U] / [CO2] 10 . Explain the 2-D DFT and its inverse transform. Describe image representation in the frequency domain. 2-DFT (2 Marks) Inverse transform (1 Mark) Describe image representation in the frequency domain. (3 Marks) [An] / [CO2] 11 . Analyze how opening and closing operations can be used for noise removal. 3 Marks each [An] / [CO3] 12 . Analyze how Otsu's method determines the optimal thresholding . Definition 2 marks. Explain between class variance,and optimal threshold selection 2 marks Explain how the selected threshold provide effective foreground background separation 2 marks [An] / [CO4] [6x5 = 30] Part C, Essay Questions, Answer any 2 questions, Each question carries 15 marks 13 . For two pixels P(x,y)and Q(s,t) calculate their Euclidean, D4 and D8 distances for given coordinate values. Definition 2 marks each. Demonstration using suitable examples 3 marks each [A] / [CO2] 14 . Analyze the fundamentals of morphological image processing. Discuss its basic concepts, terminology, and major applications with suitable examples. Definition 3 marks, basic set theory for morphological operations structuring element concept of hit miss fit, neighboring elements 6 marks, applications and Explanation- how structure or shape of object change in morphological transformations using different structuring elements 6 marks [An] / [CO3] 15 .
